content.comment_body: I'm working on a [product_name] program and encountering issues related to recursion. I can resolve some problems using a flag, but I'm curious about the differences between a standard flag and an internal flag. If anyone can share documentation or references, I'd appreciate it. Specifically, I'm wondering why the standard flag solves my recursion issue but the internal flag does not. Additionally, are there other approaches to managing recursion in the [product_name] environment besides redesigning logic to avoid it? Thanks in advance, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], If I'm correct, to enable recursion in your setup, simply place a flag after the block you want feedback from, and use the output of that flag for recursion. I'm not entirely sure if this answers your question. Best regards, [user_name] Check the attachment for a sample program. Note: You may not be able to place eight blocks in a single line; I don't recall if this restriction still applies or if it was only present in earlier versions.

I've figured out the basics of using flags. My main question is why 'internal flags' seem ineffective compared to regular flags. By the way, I'm working with ladder logic rather than function blocks. From what I understand, 'internal flags' are mainly used in ladder logic to help organize things. Can anyone confirm or correct this assumption? Regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], You are correct that internal flags aren't available in block diagrams. Unfortunately, I haven't programmed a [product_name] in ladder logic myself, so I can't provide insight into the differences between these types of flags. Sorry I couldn't be of more help. Best regards

From my understanding, an internal flag isn't treated as a flag in block diagrams. A regular flag acts as memory that retains the input through the cycle, which you need for recursive bits. An internal flag, on the other hand, functions like a simple connection between two points—meaning it provides no memory or time delay. I hope this clarifies things.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants express confusion about the differences between regular and internal flags in the [product_name] programming environment, particularly regarding recursive logic and across various programming styles such as ladder logic and block diagrams. The discussion highlights a lack of clear documentation and in-tool distinctions, leading to speculation and uncertainty around best practices for control logic design involving flags.
